mainTopic: The exemption of bought or gifted animals from מעשר בהמה: its source in the היקש to 'your son,' and its limit to animals bought when fit to be offered (purchased fetuses, אתנן bought back)
overview: The גמרא finishes a היקש: just as פדיון הבן applies only to your own son, מעשר בהמה applies only to your own animals, not ones bought or received as a gift. It then explains why the verse, which is about בכור, can teach this. The word 'כן תעשה' has no use for a בכור, which is holy from birth, so it is moved to מעשר בהמה. The גמרא tests other possible targets for the phrase: חטאת and אשם, then עולה and שלמים, then עולת ראייה. Each is ruled out because only מעשר בהמה is like 'your son' in every way: it is not for a sin, it is not a נדר or נדבה, and it has no fixed time. Next the גמרא asks why רבי אסי rules that fetuses bought in the womb are tithed. רבא and רבי אלעזר answer that 'תעשה' limits the exemption to animals bought when they are already fit to be offered. A ברייתא that seems to say otherwise is either rejected or assigned to רבי שמעון בן יהודה. Finally, an אתנן that was bought back can be tithed, because it was bought back while still a fetus.

steps.title: Your animals are like your son: nothing bought, nothing received as a gift
steps.stepSummary: The היקש is completed: מעשר בהמה, like פדיון הבן, does not apply to what was bought or received as a gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as 'your sons' does not include a son who was bought or given as a gift, so 'your flock and your herd' does not include animals that were bought or given as a gift.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a comparison (היקש) between 'your son' and 'your animals' in the same verse. The point is that only animals born into your own herd are included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse puts 'your son' next to 'your ox and your sheep.' The obligation of פדיון הבן applies only to a son who is truly yours by birth. The verse links the two, so the same limit applies to the animals: purchased or gifted animals are left out.

keyTerms.meaning: "Just as... so too...", the formula for comparing two cases
A comparison drawn because two things appear side by side in a פסוק

phrases.english: Just as 'your sons' does not apply to one bought or received as a gift,
phrases.notes: The מצוה of redeeming the firstborn son applies only to one's own child.

phrases.aramaic: אַף צֹאנְךָ וּבְקָרְךָ — אֵינוֹ בְּלָקוּחַ וּבְמַתָּנָה.
phrases.english: so too 'your flock and your herd' does not apply to animals bought or received as a gift.
phrases.notes: Here the גמרא is applying this to מעשר בהמה, the animal tithe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the derivation that began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Purchased or gifted animals are exempt from מעשר בהמה, learned from the היקש to 'your son.'

steps.title: But that verse is about the firstborn
steps.stepSummary: Challenge: the verse comparing son and animals speaks of בכור, not מעשר בהמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this verse is written about the firstborn!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects to the derivation. The verse it used talks about firstborns, so how can it teach us anything about מעשר בהמה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse reads 'the firstborn of your sons you shall give to Me; so you shall do with your oxen and your sheep.' On a plain reading, the animals there are firstborn animals, and מעשר בהמה is not mentioned at all. So the derivation seems to be pinned on the wrong topic.

keyTerms.meaning: Firstborn (here, a firstborn animal or son)

phrases.english: But this verse is written about the firstborn!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source used in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using the verse about בכור to learn about מעשר בהמה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse's subject is בכור, so the exemption should apply to firstborns, not to tithe.

steps.title: 'So you shall do' cannot mean firstborn, so it is applied to animal tithe
steps.stepSummary: Answer: the word 'do' does not fit בכור, which becomes holy at birth, so the phrase is moved to מעשר בהמה, which requires an act.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'so you shall DO.' If it cannot refer to the firstborn, since nothing is done to a firstborn because it becomes holy from the womb, apply it to animal tithe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with the rule of אם אינו ענין: if a phrase has no use in its own topic, move it to a related one. 'Do' is useless for בכור, so it is applied to מעשר בהמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור is holy automatically as it leaves the womb, and the owner does nothing to make it holy. With מעשר בהמה, the owner must actively count the animals and mark the tenth one, so 'doing' fits there. That is why the extra word is moved over to מעשר בהמה.

keyTerms.meaning: "If it is not needed for this topic", the rule that moves a phrase to another topic
An action or act of doing
The tithe of animals: every tenth animal is made holy

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is denying that a בכור is holy. It is only saying that the word 'do' adds nothing there, because the בכור's holiness happens without any act.

phrases.english: The verse says: 'So you shall do,'
if it is not relevant to the firstborn,
since it does not involve any action, because it is holy from the womb,
apply it to the matter of animal tithe.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: ״כֵּן תַּעֲשֶׂה״, אִם אֵינוֹ עִנְיָן לִבְכוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse refers only to בכור.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Do' is extra for בכור, so it teaches about מעשר בהמה, which requires an act of sanctifying.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rest of this passage. Once the phrase is 'free' to move, the גמרא has to justify why it lands on מעשר בהמה rather than some other קרבן.

steps.title: Maybe it should apply to the sin offering and guilt offering
steps.stepSummary: Challenge: why move the phrase to מעשר בהמה rather than to חטאת and אשם?
steps.simpleTranslation: But say instead: apply it to the sin offering and the guilt offering!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back. If the phrase needs a new home, why not put it on חטאת and אשם, which are also made holy by an act?
steps.deeperAnalysis: חטאת and אשם are designated by a person's action, so 'do' could fit them too. In that case the rule 'not bought, not a gift' would apply to them instead of to מעשר בהמה.

keyTerms.meaning: "But say instead...", introducing an alternative suggestion

phrases.english: But say: apply it to the matter of
the sin offering and the guilt offering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions where the redirected phrase should land.
steps.kashyaTarget: Choosing מעשר בהמה as the new topic
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Other קרבנות also involve an act, so why prefer מעשר בהמה?

steps.title: It must be like 'your son', which is not brought because of a sin
steps.stepSummary: Answer: פדיון הבן is not connected to a sin, and neither is מעשר בהמה, but חטאת and אשם are.
steps.simpleTranslation: It must be similar to 'your son.' Just as your son does not come because of a sin, so 'your sheep and your ox' must be something that does not come because of a sin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the phrase is tied to 'your son' and has to match it. חטאת and אשם come because of a sin, so they do not match.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Redeeming a son has nothing to do with sin. מעשר בהמה is also not brought for a sin. חטאת and אשם are only brought because someone sinned, so the comparison points to מעשר בהמה.

keyTerms.meaning: "Similar to...", the target must resemble the case it is compared to
Comes (is brought) because of a sin

phrases.english: It must be similar to 'your son':

phrases.aramaic: מָה בִּנְךָ שֶׁאֵינוֹ בָּא עַל חֵטְא,
phrases.english: just as your son does not come because of a sin,

phrases.aramaic: אַף צֹאנְךָ וְשׁוֹרְךָ שֶׁאֵינוֹ בָּא עַל חֵטְא.
phrases.english: so too 'your sheep and your ox' refers to something that does not come because of a sin.

steps.triggerLanguage: דּוּמְיָא דְּבִנְךָ — מָה בִּנְךָ שֶׁאֵינוֹ בָּא עַל חֵטְא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction based on similarity to the compared case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase could apply to חטאת and אשם.
steps.terutzMaskana: It must match 'your son', which is not linked to sin, so חטאת and אשם are excluded.

steps.title: Maybe it should apply to the burnt offering and peace offering
steps.stepSummary: Challenge: עולה and שלמים are not brought for a sin, so why not apply the phrase to them?
steps.simpleTranslation: But say instead: apply it to the burnt offering and the peace offering!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries again with a new suggestion. עולה and שלמים pass the 'not for a sin' test, so maybe the phrase belongs to them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 5 ruled out only sin-related offerings. עולה and שלמים can be brought without any sin, so they seem to fit the comparison as well as מעשר בהמה does.

phrases.english: But say: apply it to the matter of
the burnt offering and the peace offering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes a new candidate that survives the test from step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: Choosing מעשר בהמה over עולה and שלמים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: עולה and שלמים are also not brought for sin, so they fit the 'your son' comparison just as well.

steps.title: Your son is not a vow or a donation, and neither is animal tithe
steps.stepSummary: Answer: 'your son' cannot be a נדר or נדבה, and neither can מעשר בהמה, but עולה and שלמים can.
steps.simpleTranslation: It must be similar to 'your son.' Just as your son does not come through a vow or a voluntary gift, so 'your sheep and your ox' (and the rest of the comparison).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא again uses the 'like your son' test, now with a second feature. Since עולה and שלמים can be brought by vow or donation, they do not match. The next step tries one more candidate that passes both tests.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nobody has a son through a vow or as a voluntary donation. In the same way, מעשר בהמה is a fixed obligation and cannot be brought by נדר or נדבה. עולה and שלמים are often brought that way, so they are ruled out.

keyTerms.meaning: A vow to bring an offering ("I take upon myself...")
A voluntary donation of a specific animal
"Etc.", the rest of the formula is understood

steps.whatToRemember: The exemption of bought or gifted animals from מעשר בהמה comes from the היקש to 'your son.' 'כן תעשה' is moved from בכור, which needs no act, to מעשר בהמה. It cannot go to חטאת or אשם, which are brought for sin, or to עולה or שלמים, which can be a נדר or נדבה. Step 8 raises one more candidate, and step 9 rules it out with a third test.

phrases.english: It must be similar to 'your son':

phrases.aramaic: מָה בִּנְךָ שֶׁאֵינוֹ בָּא בְּנֶדֶר וּנְדָבָה,
phrases.english: just as your son does not come through a vow or a voluntary gift,
so too 'your sheep and your ox,' etc.
phrases.notes: This is talking about מעשר בהמה, which also can't be a vow or a gift.

steps.triggerLanguage: דּוּמְיָא דְּבִנְךָ — מָה בִּנְךָ שֶׁאֵינוֹ בָּא בְּנֶדֶר וּנְדָבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 6. One more candidate is still tested in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Second point of similarity to the compared case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase could apply to עולה and שלמים.
steps.terutzMaskana: עולה and שלמים are excluded because they can be brought as a נדר or נדבה, unlike 'your son.'

steps.title: Why not apply the phrase to the burnt offering of appearance?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the phrase could refer to עולת ראייה, which is not brought for a sin and is not a נדר or נדבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say instead: apply the phrase to the burnt offering of appearance!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises one more possible candidate for the verse's phrase. This is עולת ראייה, which passes both earlier tests.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 ruled out חטאת and אשם because they come for a sin. Step 7 ruled out עולה and שלמים because they can be a נדר or נדבה. עולת ראייה is an obligation and is not tied to a sin, so it seems to fit just as well as מעשר בהמה.

keyTerms.meaning: Apply it as a matter for (redirect the verse to another topic)
The burnt offering brought when one goes up to Jerusalem on the three festivals

phrases.english: But say: apply it as a matter
phrases.notes: He means: use the extra words to teach about a different topic.

phrases.english: for the burnt offering of appearance!
phrases.notes: This offering isn't brought for a sin and isn't a vow or gift, so it fits both earlier tests.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the process of elimination after Step 7 ruled out עולה and שלמים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice to apply the phrase to מעשר בהמה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: עולת ראייה matches בנך on both features named so far (no sin, not a נדר or נדבה), so nothing yet explains choosing מעשר בהמה over it.

steps.title: Your son and animal tithe have no fixed time
steps.stepSummary: Like redeeming a son, מעשר בהמה has no fixed time of year, but עולת ראייה is tied to the festivals.
steps.simpleTranslation: It must be similar to 'your son'. Just as your son has no fixed time, so too 'your oxen and your sheep' refers to something that has no fixed time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that there is one more way that מעשר בהמה is like בנך. Neither has a fixed date, while עולת ראייה does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A son is redeemed after thirty days from his birth, whenever that happens to be. מעשר בהמה is likewise not tied to a calendar date. עולת ראייה is brought only on the three festivals, so it is less similar to בנך and is ruled out.

keyTerms.meaning: Your son (the פדיון הבן part of the verse)

steps.whatToRemember: The phrase goes to מעשר בהמה because it matches בנך on every test. It is not for a sin, it cannot be a נדר or נדבה, and it has no fixed time.

phrases.english: It must be similar to 'your son'

phrases.aramaic: מָה בִּנְךָ שֶׁאֵין קָבוּעַ לוֹ זְמַן
phrases.english: just as your son has no fixed time
phrases.notes: A son is redeemed 30 days after birth, whenever that happens to fall.

phrases.english: so too 'your oxen and your sheep'
refers to something that has no fixed time
phrases.notes: מעשר בהמה fits this, but עולת ראייה is tied to the festivals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 8's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds another feature of the comparison to בנך that excludes the competing candidate.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: עולת ראייה matches בנך just as well as מעשר בהמה does.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only מעשר בהמה shares בנך's lack of a fixed time, so the phrase applies to it.

steps.title: If it is like a son, a purchased animal should never be tithed
steps.stepSummary: If מעשר בהמה is compared to בנך, then no purchased animal should ever be tithed. That contradicts רבי אסי's ruling that purchased fetuses are tithed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, just as your son cannot be purchased at all, so too your oxen and sheep should not be tithed if purchased in any way. Then why did רבי אסי say in the name of רבי יוחנן: if one bought ten fetuses in their mothers' wombs, they all enter the pen to be tithed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes the comparison to בנך all the way. It then shows that this clashes with a known ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A firstborn son is never 'purchased', so the comparison suggests that any purchase at all should exempt an animal. Yet רבי אסי rules that fetuses bought while still in the womb are tithed once they are born. The comparison seems to prove too much.

keyTerms.meaning: If just as (pushes a comparison to its full extent)
The pen where animals are counted for tithing

steps.confusionAlert: The fetuses are tithed after they are born. They enter the pen as born animals, but they were bought while still in the womb.

phrases.aramaic: אִי מָה בִּנְךָ אֵינוֹ בְּלָקוּחַ כְּלָל
phrases.english: If so, just as your son cannot be purchased at all

phrases.aramaic: אַף שׁוֹרְךָ וְצֹאנְךָ אֵינוֹ בְּלָקוּחַ כְּלָל
phrases.english: so too your oxen and sheep should not be tithed if purchased at all

phrases.aramaic: אַלְּמָה אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Why then did Rabbi Asi say in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
If one bought ten fetuses in their mothers' wombs
they all enter the pen to be tithed?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מָה בִּנְךָ אֵינוֹ בְּלָקוּחַ כְּלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the comparison to בנך that was just established and pushes it to an extreme.
steps.kashyaTarget: The full comparison between מעשר בהמה and בנך.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the comparison is complete, then every purchased animal should be exempt. But רבי אסי rules that purchased fetuses are tithed.

steps.title: The exemption applies only at the 'time of doing'
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the word תעשה limits the exemption to animals that were already purchased when they were fit to be offered. Fetuses do not fall into that category.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the verse says 'you shall do'. The verse excluded only an animal that was purchased at the time of 'doing'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the contradiction by reading the word 'do' in the verse closely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The exemption for purchased animals applies only if the animal was bought at the stage of 'doing', meaning when it is a born animal fit for the מזבח. A fetus is not yet at that stage. So buying it in the womb does not exempt it, and רבי אסי's ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: At the time of doing (when the animal is fit to be offered)

steps.whyThisMatters: The same word תעשה that moved the phrase away from בכור in Step 3 now also limits how far the exemption for purchased animals reaches.

phrases.english: Rava said: the verse says:
'you shall do'
the verse excluded only a purchase at the time of doing
phrases.notes: A fetus is not yet fit to be offered, so buying it does not exempt it

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 10's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A close reading of the verse limits the scope of the exemption.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any purchase at all exempts the animal, as with בנך.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only animals that were purchased at the stage when they are fit to be offered are exempt. Fetuses bought in the womb are tithed.

steps.title: רבי אסי's ruling quoted on its own
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי אסי's ruling in full so that it can examine it directly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the matter itself. רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: if one bought ten fetuses in their mothers' wombs, they all enter the pen to be tithed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new discussion about רבי אסי's ruling itself. This is a setup line that prepares a challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling was only mentioned in passing in Step 10. The word גופא signals that the גמרא now turns to analyze it directly.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself (returns to examine a statement quoted earlier)

phrases.english: The matter itself:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
If one bought ten fetuses in their mothers' wombs
they all enter the pen to be tithed.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא, אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns back to the ruling that Step 10 cited, now as a topic of its own.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fetuses bought in the womb are subject to מעשר בהמה once they are born.

steps.title: The משנה says purchased animals are exempt
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a purchased animal or one received as a gift is exempt from מעשר בהמה. That seems to contradict רבי אסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in the משנה: one who buys an animal, or receives one as a gift, is exempt from animal tithe!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אסי's ruling from a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה exempts purchased animals with no qualification. רבי אסי obligates purchased fetuses. The question is why fetuses should be different from the general rule of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: But we learned in a משנה (introduces a challenge from a משנה)

phrases.english: But we learned in the Mishnah:
One who buys, or to whom it was given as a gift,
is exempt from animal tithe!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling quoted in Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אסי's ruling that purchased fetuses are tithed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה exempts every purchased animal without exception, so purchased fetuses should also be exempt.

steps.title: Purchase exemption applies only once the animal is fit to be offered
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר defends רבי אסי. The word תעשה teaches that the purchase exemption applies only to animals bought at the 'time of doing,' meaning when they are fit to be offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: I saw רבי יוחנן in a dream, so I am about to say something good. The verse says 'you shall do' (תעשה). This teaches that the verse excluded purchased animals only when they were bought at the time they could be 'done,' meaning offered.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers the challenge from the משנה (step 13). He explains that the משנה's exemption for purchased animals applies only to animals bought when they were already fit to be offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה exempts purchased animals, but רבי אלעזר limits that exemption to animals bought at the 'time of doing.' A fetus bought in its mother's womb was not yet fit for anything. So it is not covered by the exemption, and רבי אסי's ruling does not contradict the משנה. The dream of רבי יוחנן is mentioned as a sign that this explanation is correct.

keyTerms.meaning: At the time of 'doing,' i.e., when the animal is fit to be offered

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
I saw Rabbi Yochanan in a dream,
phrases.notes: Seeing a great sage in a dream is taken as a good sign.

phrases.english: so I will say a fine statement.
The verse says: 'you shall do,'
phrases.notes: שמות כב:כט, the verse the גמרא used to compare מעשר בהמה to בכור and בנך.

phrases.english: the verse excluded only at the time of 'doing.'
phrases.notes: Only animals purchased when already fit to be offered are exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן חֲזַאי בְּחֶילְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the משנה in step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the משנה's exemption through a verse
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה exempts every purchased animal, including fetuses, which would contradict רבי אסי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The exemption covers only animals bought when already fit to be offered. Fetuses are tithed.

steps.title: A ברייתא applies the purchase exemption even to an underage animal
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אליקים objects from a ברייתא. It says the purchase exemption applies even to an animal that is still מחוסר זמן (too young to be offered).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אליקים challenged רבי אלעזר: 'The purchase exemption applies even to an animal that is not yet old enough!'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן אליקים challenges רבי אלעזר's limit. He quotes a source showing that the exemption applies even before the animal is fit to be offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר said the exemption starts only at the 'time of doing.' The ברייתא says an animal bought while still too young, before eight days old, is already exempt. If so, a purchased fetus should also be exempt, which goes against רבי אסי.

keyTerms.meaning: The purchased animal (exempt from מעשר בהמה)
An animal lacking time, i.e., under eight days old and not yet fit to be offered

phrases.aramaic: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְיָקִים לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elyakim raised an objection to Rabbi Elazar:
The purchase exemption applies even to an animal whose time has not yet come!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְיָקִים לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the limit רבי אלעזר set in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's claim that the exemption applies only at the 'time of doing.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A source exempts an underage purchased animal. That shows the exemption is not tied to fitness for offering, so purchased fetuses should also be exempt.

steps.title: The ברייתא is not a reliable source
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר answers that this ברייתא is not an authoritative teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is not a reliable משנה (teaching).
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר's first response is to reject the source itself. He says the ברייתא is not a dependable teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of explaining the ברייתא, רבי אלעזר questions whether it is accurate at all. If the source is not reliable, it cannot be used to challenge his reading of תעשה.

keyTerms.meaning: This is not an authoritative teaching (not reliable)

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'מִשְׁנָה' does not mean 'the משנה' in our tractate. It means any reliable tannaitic teaching, including a ברייתא.

phrases.english: He said to him:
This is not a reliable teaching,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the challenge in step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the authority of the ברייתא quoted in step 15.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא is not an accurate or authoritative tannaitic source.

steps.title: Even if reliable, the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון בן יהודה
steps.stepSummary: Even if the ברייתא is reliable, it follows רבי שמעון בן יהודה in the name of רבי שמעון. He holds that an underage animal already counts for tithing, just as a בכור is holy before it is old enough to be offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you insist it is a reliable teaching, it follows רבי שמעון בן יהודה in the name of רבי שמעון. He says an underage animal enters the pen to be tithed. It is like a בכור: just as a בכור becomes holy before its time but is offered after its time, so too an underage animal becomes holy before its time and is offered after its time.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives a second answer. Even if the ברייתא is accepted, it fits only the opinion of רבי שמעון בן יהודה, who treats an underage animal as already part of the tithing process.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון בן יהודה, a living animal under eight days old already enters the pen and can become מעשר. For him, it is already at the 'time of doing' for tithing purposes, so the purchase exemption applies to it. A fetus is not even born, so it is still not covered, and רבי אסי's ruling is unaffected.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you insist on saying
Enters the pen to be tithed
A firstborn animal, holy from birth

keyTerms.term: קָדוֹשׁ לִפְנֵי זְמַנּוֹ וְקָרֵב לְאַחַר זְמַנּוֹ
keyTerms.meaning: Holy before its time, but offered only after its time

phrases.english: And if you insist it is a reliable teaching,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה הִיא מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן,
phrases.english: it is the opinion of Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda in the name of Rabbi Shimon,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: מְחוּסַּר זְמַן נִכְנָס לַדִּיר לְהִתְעַשֵּׂר,
phrases.english: who says: an animal whose time has not come enters the pen to be tithed,
and it is like a firstborn:
just as a firstborn is holy before its time
and is offered after its time,

phrases.aramaic: אַף מְחוּסַּר זְמַן קָדוֹשׁ לִפְנֵי זְמַנּוֹ
phrases.english: so too an animal whose time has not come is holy before its time
and is offered after its time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second answer to step 15. It accepts the ברייתא but limits it to one תנא's view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the source to a specific minority opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא proves the exemption applies before the animal is fit, even to fetuses.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא reflects רבי שמעון בן יהודה, for whom an underage animal already counts for tithing. A fetus is still not covered.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the 'time of doing' depends on when the animal becomes part of tithing. That point ties together רבי אלעזר's reading and רבי אסי's ruling.

steps.title: A ברייתא about an אתנן that is bought back
steps.stepSummary: A תנא teaches before רב that the אתנן which enters the pen to be tithed is one that was given to a זונה and then bought back from her.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא taught before רב: Which אתנן enters the pen to be tithed? Any animal that he gave to her and then bought back from her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about an אתנן (an animal given as payment to a זונה). It is setting up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא defines which אתנן can still be tithed: one the man gave and then bought back. That seems strange, because buying it back makes it a purchased animal, which should be exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: A reciter of ברייתות taught in front of רב
Payment given to a זונה, which is forbidden as an offering

phrases.english: A tanna taught before Rav:
Which is the prostitute's payment
that enters the pen to be tithed?
Any animal that he gave to her
and then bought back from her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a new source that will raise another purchase question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אתנן that was given and then bought back enters the pen to be tithed.

steps.title: Buying back the אתנן should make it exempt
steps.stepSummary: The question is raised: once he buys it back, it is a purchased animal and should be disqualified from tithing.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is disqualified because it is a purchased animal!
steps.whatsHappening: Someone challenges the ברייתא just quoted. Buying the animal back makes it a לקוח, which should be exempt from tithing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that purchased animals are not tithed. The ברייתא's case involves buying the animal back from the זונה, so the animal should be exempt. That makes the ברייתא's ruling look impossible.

phrases.english: But it is disqualified as a purchased animal!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of the ברייתא in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that an אתנן bought back is tithed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Buying it back makes it a purchased animal, and purchased animals are exempt from מעשר בהמה.

steps.title: The questioner forgot רבי אסי's ruling on purchased fetuses
steps.stepSummary: The questioner forgot רבי אסי's ruling in the name of רבי יוחנן: purchased fetuses are tithed. So the ברייתא is talking about an אתנן bought back while it was still a fetus.
steps.simpleTranslation: He forgot what רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: If someone bought ten fetuses while still in their mothers' wombs, they all enter the pen to be tithed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the questioner forgot רבי אסי's ruling. With that ruling, the ברייתא makes sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Purchased fetuses are tithed, because they were bought before the 'time of doing.' So the ברייתא can be read as an אתנן given and bought back while still in its mother's womb. That purchase does not disqualify it, and the case also supports רבי אסי's ruling from earlier in the סוגיא.
steps.whatToRemember: The purchase exemption from מעשר בהמה applies only to an animal bought when it was already fit to be offered. Fetuses bought in the womb are tithed (רבי אסי). That is why an אתנן bought back while still a fetus can be tithed.

phrases.english: It escaped him

phrases.aramaic: הָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: that which Rabbi Asi said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
If one bought ten fetuses in their mothers' wombs,
they all enter the pen to be tithed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִישְׁתְּמִיטְתֵּיהּ הָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 19 by using רבי אסי's ruling.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-defining the case (an animal bought back while still a fetus)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any animal bought back is a לקוח and is exempt from tithing.
steps.terutzMaskana: An animal bought back while still a fetus is not exempt, so the ברייתא's אתנן is tithed.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows רבי אסי's ruling at work. It also closes the סוגיא's question about how purchased fetuses fit with the purchase exemption.
